transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Um... I guess I'm mostly here because I haven't really been sleeping. Not since... well, I had to do a warehouse inspection for work recently. 

I just kind of lie in bed replaying bits of it. And if I do manage to drift off, I just... I wake up sweating. Wide awake. Like I'm right back near that blast. So... yeah. That's why I came in.
Can you tell me more about what you mean by 'I'm right back near that blast' when you wake up sweating?

Um... I just mean it feels really real. Like my body reacts before I can even stop it. 

It actually... it happens during the day, too. I'll just be sitting there reviewing a policy or looking at a loss report, and suddenly I just get hit with this really sharp image of... of the worker on the floor. And the soot in the air. So... yeah. That's what I mean.
You mentioned getting hit with a sharp image of the worker on the floor during the day, is that something you feel like you're reliving, like it's happening again?

Um... I don't really know. I guess I wouldn't say it feels like it's happening all over again. I know I'm still at my desk. It's just... a really strong picture in my head. It just throws me off for a minute. That's about it.
Have you been trying to avoid things that remind you of the warehouse inspection or the blast?

Um... I guess a little. I just... I haven't really touched that warehouse file. And, um... if I get calls about other industrial accounts, I've just been letting them go to voicemail. I don't know, even just seeing those emails in my inbox makes my stomach drop. So... yeah. I just leave them for now.
How long have you been experiencing these strong images and sleep disturbances since the warehouse inspection?
Um... about a week. Basically since the day of the inspection. Ever since the... the explosion.
Have you been startled more easily than usual since the warehouse inspection?

Um... yeah, I guess. Just... little things. Like if a door slams, or the printer jams... or if someone just walks up behind my desk. I just... I jump. Like something terrible is happening. And, um... it takes me a few minutes to settle down after that. So... yeah.
Have you been trying to push away or avoid thoughts or feelings about the warehouse inspection or the blast?
Um... I don't really know. I just... I try to stay busy, I guess. I don't really sit around thinking about it on purpose. It's just... I just try to do my work.
Do you feel guilty or responsible in any way for what happened during the warehouse inspection?

Um... no. Not really. I mean, I was just there to look at the paperwork and the inventory. I didn't... I didn't have anything to do with the machinery or the safety protocols. So... no, I don't think it was my fault.
Are there any activities or places that you've completely stopped doing or going to because they remind you of the warehouse inspection?

Um... well, at work, I guess. I've been... avoiding the file for that warehouse. And if I get calls about other industrial accounts, I just... let them go to voicemail. I don't know, just even opening those emails makes my stomach drop. So... yeah. I just leave them.
Have you avoided talking to anyone about what happened during the warehouse inspection?
Um... yeah, I guess so. I mean, my supervisor asked if I was okay, and I just... told him I was fine. I haven't really talked to anyone else about it. I just... I don't really want to get into it.
Have you stopped doing anything outside of work because it reminds you of the warehouse inspection?
Um... no. Not really. I mean... I mostly just go straight home anyway. So... I don't think there's anything outside of work that I've stopped doing. Just the work stuff.
Have you avoided talking to friends or family about the warehouse inspection?

Um... yeah. I haven't brought it up with them. I just... like I was saying earlier, I'm mostly just trying not to deal with it at work. Just... avoiding that specific warehouse file, and letting those industrial calls go straight to voicemail. Just looking at those emails makes my stomach drop, so... I definitely don't want to talk about it at home, either.
Have you lost interest in activities that you normally enjoy since the warehouse inspection?
Um... no. I don't think so. I mean, I still do my usual stuff when I get home. I haven't really noticed a change with that.
Do you find yourself constantly on the lookout for potential dangers or threats, even when you're not in a situation that would normally be considered dangerous?
Um... no. I don't think so. I haven't really noticed being on the lookout for anything like that. I just... feel normal in that way, I guess.
Have you been avoiding people, places, or activities outside of work because they remind you of the warehouse inspection or make you feel uncomfortable?
Um... no. Not really. I just go about my normal routine outside of work. I haven't been avoiding anything else.
Have you been avoiding memories or thoughts about the warehouse inspection?

Um... I guess so. At work, at least. I've just been... avoiding the actual warehouse file. And if I get calls about other industrial accounts, I just let them go to voicemail. I don't know, just... even seeing those emails makes my stomach drop. So I just try not to look at them.
Have you been avoiding people at work because they remind you of the warehouse inspection?
Um... no. Not really. I just... I still talk to my coworkers. I haven't been avoiding them or anything. I just... I just don't want to deal with the files, that's all.
Would you say that avoiding the warehouse file and industrial account calls has significantly impacted your ability to do your job?

Yeah... I suppose it has. I mean... I've missed a few deadlines recently. Just on some underwriting reviews. And... since I've been handing off those industrial calls to other people—calls I'm supposed to be managing—it's... well. I just took on this role, so... it's probably making me look pretty unreliable.
